extraction.name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series)
extraction.description: PASTIS is the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations. It is comprised of 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10x128x128. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels. Each pixel is associated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class, and each non-background pixel has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. The dataset spans over 4000 km2, with images taken from four different regions of France with diverse climates and crop distributions.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu
extraction.citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu. Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV, 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The PASTIS dataset is composed of 2,433 square 128x128 patches with 10 spectral bands and at 10m resolution, obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform. For each patch, all available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019 were stacked, forming four-dimensional multi-spectral SITS. The publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) was used to retrieve the extent and content of all parcels within the tiles, as reported by the farmers. Each patch pixel is annotated with a semantic label corresponding to either the parcels’ crop type or the background class, and pixels of each unique parcel receive a corresponding instance label.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The time between acquisitions is uneven with a median of 5 days. This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA. The policy of Sentinel data providers is not to process tile observations identified as covered by clouds for more than 90% of the tile’s surface. Even after this automatic filtering, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral images from the Sentinel-2 satellite and parcel information from the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. Specifically, bands B01, B09, and B10 were excluded. The parcels’ extents were cropped along the extent of their 128x128 patch, and bounding boxes were modified accordingly. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label. No further pre-processing or cloud detection was applied to the raw data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel of PASTIS is associated with a semantic label taken from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS). The FLPIS allows retrieval of the extent and content of all parcels within the tiles, as reported by the farmers. Classes with at least 400 parcels and with samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles were selected, leading to an 18-class nomenclature.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are annotated with the void label. The void class is reserved for out-of-scope parcels (due to crop type not in nomenclature or small overlap with patch) and these parcels are removed from all semantic or panoptic metrics and losses. Predicted parcels which overlap with an IoU superior to 0.5 with a void parcel are ignored by the metric.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each pixel has a semantic label and, for non-background pixels, a unique instance label. Each of the 124,422 individualized parcels has a bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Pixel-precise panoptic segmentation of agricultural parcels has major economic and environmental implications. Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and in the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. The automated analysis of SITS is also of significant interest for applications such as surveying urban development and deforestation. The economic and environmental stakes of panoptic SITS segmentation cannot be understated.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. To mitigate this, patches were selected favoring those with rare crop types to decrease the extreme class imbalance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The temporal sampling of the sequences in PASTIS is irregular. Even after automatic filtering, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover. The panoptic metrics are not computed for the background class, as the focus is on retrieving parcel extent rather than extensive land-cover prediction. The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, testing, and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on Satellite Image Time Series (SITS). It is split into 5 folds for cross-validation, with a 1km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination, and geographically consistent folds are possible for evaluating spatial generalization.
